name: dsh
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 against DeepSeek Harness Desktop 0.2.2-rc.3 on Windows 11, from dsh's own installed documentation and sources plus a live session. (1) USER-GLOBAL RULES: dsh-agent-instructions composes the user-global chain as $DSH_HOME/AGENTS.md first, then <agentsHome>/AGENTS.md ($DSH_AGENTS_HOME or ~/.agents) — the standard preset mounts it with maxBytes 65536 — so .dsh/AGENTS.md is the managed target, and ~/.agents/AGENTS.md is the user-owned overlay slot for machine-specific additions (editing the managed file is what `apply` reverts). (2) SKILLS: ~/.agents/skills is a native user skill root; project .agents/skills overrides it and the packaged preset skill overrides both, so the same link pi uses is enough — this manifest declares no skill dimension on purpose. (3) PLUGINS: dsh does NOT auto-load an extensions directory; a row has to be mounted through the Cordis composition, which is why gates/commands declare auto_load false and carry a verified patch row. An installed plugin directory also needs package.json {"type":"module"} because these plugins are ES modules (bridge/lib/gates.js and bridge/lib/commands.js write it). (4) COMMANDS: dsh registers slash commands from plugins (`ctx.commands.register`), and ships no prompt-template directory, so Claude's command files are only reachable through the plugin this target installs (dsh/commands/), which copies them into prompts/*.md and injects one as the user's next prompt through `agent.followup()`. (5) MCP: dsh has NO global mcp.json equivalent. Live servers live in the profile's cordis.patch.yml under the `mcp-manager` row's config.servers (transport/command/args/env/cwd/enabled, secrets as ${credential:NAME} templates resolved from ~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml refs), and that file is a settings surface the GUI also writes. This target therefore declares NO mcp dimension: the profile tree is never_touch, and guessing a path here is how a bridge silently writes a file nobody reads.

managed.note: the fixed user-global instruction file dsh-agent-instructions loads first, before the shared agents root. Because `apply` owns this file, machine-specific DSH additions belong in ~/.agents/AGENTS.md (loaded second, never written by this project) rather than in edits here.

the prompt templates behind the installed slash-command plugin. dsh has no prompt-template directory: the plugin (dsh/commands/index.js) reads this directory at activation and registers one command per file, injecting the rendered template as the user's next prompt. Copied from ~/.claude/commands so the prompt text stays owned by the user and by Claude Code.

gates.mount_hint:
dsh mounts plugins through a Cordis composition, so an installed directory takes effect only when a row points at it. Add this to the profile patch (~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml; `node scripts/install-dsh.js --yes` writes it and prints this snippet):

- insert:
    - id: enforce-rules
      # relative specifier, anchored beside the patch file; a file:// URL also works
      name: '../../plugins/agent-config-gates/dsh/index.js'
      config:
        policyPath: '<absolute>/.dsh/plugins/agent-config-gates/policy.json'

status reports whether the gate directory is installed; whether it is mounted is visible only in the composition file, which this project deliberately does not edit.

commands.mount_hint:
- insert:
    - id: agent-config-commands
      # relative specifier, anchored beside the patch file
      name: '../../plugins/agent-config-commands/index.js'
